supporting_passage: Variable formats, schemas and modalities limit the interoperability of data offered to a data space. The framework converts inputs to RDF under an input ontology and records provenance.
note: Publisher abstract consulted. It identifies a concrete mismatch before presenting the transformation method.

sentence: [Lazarotto2022] assess business-to-government access under the Data Act proposal, and [Tyagi2026] ask what the Digital Markets Act and the Data Act contribute to cloud sovereignty and contestability.
supporting_passage: The analysis examines whether EU obligations can improve contestability where technical complexity, egress fees and ecosystem lock-in make it difficult for cloud customers to switch.
note: Institutional abstract consulted. T2 also fits the interoperability dimension of cloud switching.

subsection: RQ3: Interoperability in Sovereign Data Spaces
sentence: [OttoJarke2019] describe how stakeholder groups used governance mechanisms during the design of the IDS platform, and report that the initiative treated trust and data sovereignty as more relevant regulatory instruments than pricing.
supporting_passage: The three-year IDS case found that stakeholders emphasized trust and control over data as governance instruments during platform design, with pricing less central at that stage.
note: Repository article abstract consulted. This row concerns reported design choices.

sentence: [Jung2022] describe usage control that continues after access, using provenance, and note that it relies on the trust placed in the endpoint.
supporting_passage: Usage control relies on the component processing the data to enforce policy. Provenance provides a way to track use and check adherence downstream.
note: Chapter body consulted. Trust in the enforcement endpoint is an operational assumption.

sentence: The work on the European Health Data Space covers interoperability and governance [Terzis2023], portability rights [LiQuinn2024], anonymization and secure processing environments [Rak2024], certification against cyber threats [Casarosa2024], emergency data sharing between the GDPR, the Data Governance Act, and the Health Data Space [Parziale2025], and citizen engagement [CerveraDeLaCruz2026].
supporting_passage: Ambiguity in the definition and scope of secondary-use health data could lead to inconsistent application of anonymization, pseudonymization and secure-processing safeguards.
note: Publisher abstract consulted. The reported limitation is legal and concerns implementation.

subsection: RQ4: Research Gaps, Limitations, and Challenges
sentence: Sector studies illustrate the unevenness: [Xia2024] discuss governance and human-rights challenges of cross-border health data flows, [Arroyo2025] question the emergency readiness of the European Health Data Space, and [Borowicz2024] examine data quality obligations in the European Financial Data Space.
supporting_passage: Divergent European, US and Chinese rules can make health data harder to share for joint research and telemedicine, with consequences for privacy and access.
note: Publisher abstract consulted. The passage concerns the effects of different regimes on cross-border work.

sentence: The work on the European Health Data Space covers interoperability and governance [Terzis2023], portability rights [LiQuinn2024], anonymization and secure processing environments [Rak2024], certification against cyber threats [Casarosa2024], emergency data sharing between the GDPR, the Data Governance Act, and the Health Data Space [Parziale2025], and citizen engagement [CerveraDeLaCruz2026].

note: Abstract consulted. The citation supports the combination of federated learning and blockchain.

subsection: RQ4: Research Gaps, Limitations, and Challenges
sentence: Many contributions are conceptual or tested only as proofs of concept or single cases [Schleimer2023,Firdausy2022c,Hmimou2025,Santana2025,Fotiou2026], and the most recent mapping study covers the literature only up to its own search cutoff [Kovach2026].

sentence: [Carovano2023] examine how the Act regulates intermediaries and what this means for the data economy, [vonDitfurth2022] ask whether it promotes or restricts them, and [Azcoitia2026] examine the neutrality and competitiveness of intermediaries under the Act.

sentence: Connector integration with industrial and telecom standards & Technical; APIs and information models & Links connectors to AAS, FIWARE, and TM Forum interfaces & [Inigo2022,Ahle2022,Choque2026]
supporting_passage: The FIWARE BAE transaction ends with the purchase and lacks bilateral usage-term negotiation. Linking it to EDC requires adding contract negotiation and post-purchase controls to the workflow.
note: Article body consulted. The integration bridges a gap between the telecom marketplace and IDS connector capabilities.

sentence: Connector certification and remote trust were discussed by [Huber2022].
supporting_passage: The IDS security concept combines connector and environment certification with public-key certificates and verification of connector identity and software integrity.
note: Abstract consulted. The passage sets out trust requirements and their implementation design.

sentence: For the Data Act, [Casolari2023] provide a legal assessment that compares approaches to the regulation of Internet-of-Things data, [Straub2025] discuss its effect on corporate digital sovereignty, and [Drechsler2025] compare the notion of fairness in the two instruments.
supporting_passage: The authors identify strengths and shortcomings in the Data Act and compare EU rules for IoT data with the approaches taken in the United States and China.
note: Institutional abstract consulted. The cited comparison identifies possible synergies and conflicts at the legal-framework level.

sentence: [Holfelder2022] describe sovereign cloud technologies for data spaces, and [Fotiou2025Proxies] study semi-trusted proxies.

note: Author manuscript abstract consulted. The cited point is the proxy architecture.
